subject: Small current-source tests for Foundation borrow planning
claim: Sixteen bounded borrow-planner cases passed on Windows. Creating the small native package took 10,748 ms; the final warm runner completed in 1,691 ms, including cleanup. A temporary source defect rebuilt its products and failed with the expected native case result 2 rather than reusing passing behavior. This claim excludes compiler integration and candidate WVB 1.39 admission.

source.value: Worktree based on 3c781190b8260e481910e19b09e8c463c6092f47. The final warm run inputs are identified below. The initial package-creation observation used the preceding synchronous runner with the same planner, fixture, project, and WVB bytes; the runner was then refactored to share bounded asynchronous child-process handling. The deliberate planner mutation was removed before the warm run.

runs.target: Sixteen planner cases, first native package construction in the existing cache
Temporarily clear borrowed-load provenance; require native case result 2 and wrapper rejection. Changed project construction took 1,795 ms and changed native packaging 10,930 ms.
runs.command: Tools\Native\Test-Language-1.0-Memory-Budget-Split-Execution.cmd --foundation-borrow-plan; require exit 1 after seeded source defect

runs.target: Restored planner, content-keyed product reuse, fresh native execution of all sixteen cases, and cleanup
Final changed-file dispatch with owner-result reuse disabled: selected planner ran all sixteen cases in 1,296 ms; complete command including classification and editor check finished in 3,779 ms
Shared child-process implementation: all 329 existing front-end development claims, with fresh behavioral execution
Final contracts, positive and excluded planner selections, shared runner fault checks, declared development dependencies, 31 general routing cases, and 280 native routing cases
Approved twenty-minute candidate publication attempt, interrupted after completing only the pinned analyzer package when the remaining cold plan was disproportionate

limitations: These are local development observations, not stable performance thresholds, clean-machine bootstrap timings, Linux reproduction, or cross-host qualification.

The draft cross-call WVB writer, new structural publication probes, complete WVB 1.39 verification, scalar execution, native lowering, WebAssembly, and consumer migration are not validated by these planner cases. The complete 208-case owner was not run.

An initial test source used duplicate function-local names and was rejected before execution; those names were repaired. The bounded interpreter then exited 66. The retained check uses the ordinary native test path without increasing interpreter or compiler limits.
The planner consumes already validated WVIR and declaration-derived parameter/call masks. Its index and allocation checks are not a replacement for full WVIR or WVB admission.

The interrupted publication attempt used the earlier writer and synchronous runner, before extracting the pure planner. Its completed 50,753,536-byte pinned analyzer package remains cached; partial packages and the interrupted attempt are not passing evidence.
Peak memory was not measured for the small native planner check. It enforces 4,096 operations, temporaries, and slots, and bounded input ranges. No seeded defect remains in the source.
